item.research_question: How does increasing copper content (x = 0 to 1.0) affect the microstructure and electrochemical corrosion resistance of lightweight AlCrTiV0.5Cux high-entropy alloys in a 0.6 M NaCl solution?
item.processing_route: Vacuum arc melting in a graphite crucible under Ar atmosphere; raw materials (Al 99.5%, Cr 99.95%, Ti 99.95%, V 99.95%, Cu 99.95%) remelted at least six times; samples ground with grit-2000 SiC sandpaper and ultrasonically cleaned in ethanol.
item.test_conditions: Electrochemical tests at 25 °C in 0.6 M NaCl solution with air exposure; potentiodynamic polarization scan rate 3 mV/s from −0.9 to 1.1 VSHE; EIS with 5 mV amplitude from 100 kHz to 10 MHz; working electrode area 0.25 cm2.
key_findings: AlCrTiV0.5 exhibited the highest corrosion resistance with a self-corrosion current density (Icorr) of 0.131 μA/cm2.
AlCrTiV0.5Cu (x=1.0) exhibited the lowest corrosion resistance with an Icorr of 2.778 μA/cm2.
Charge transfer resistance (R3) decreased from 437,920 Ω·cm2 for AlCrTiV0.5 to 31,276 Ω·cm2 for AlCrTiV0.5Cu.
Microstructure transitioned from equiaxed single-phase BCC (x=0) to dendritic structures with FCC phases and intermetallic compounds as Cu increased.
Cu segregation at grain boundaries increased with Cu content, leading to the formation of Al-Ti-Cu-rich HCP phases and V-Cr-rich FCC phases.
Corrosion morphology showed smooth surfaces for AlCrTiV0.5, while Cu-added alloys developed enormous corrosion pits in dendritic intergranular regions.
The corrosion resistance decreased monotonically as the copper content increased from 0 to 1.0.
item.mechanism: The addition of Cu causes segregation at grain boundaries, creating Cu-rich and Cu-depleted regions with significant potential differences. This leads to galvanic coupling where the interdendritic (Cu-rich) area corrodes first. While sluggish diffusion and high-entropy effects can inhibit corrosion in the absence of segregation, the presence of Cu-rich areas exposed to the surface negates these benefits, accelerating local corrosion.
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study, though it notes that the beneficial effect of slow diffusion was not obvious due to Cu segregation and that the high-entropy effect had little impact when segregation was high.
quotes: The segregation of Cu lead to a large potential difference between the Cu-rich and Cu-poor phases that formed between and within the dendrites, making the area between the dendrites more susceptible to galvanic coupling corrosion.
AlCrTiV0.5 has the lowest self-corrosion current density and the best corrosion resistance.
